items.title: Snap and crackle but no pop: Rice Krispies reformulated due to lack of rice
items.desc: Kellogg’s substitutes ingredient with rice flour, as climate crisis affects availability of some grains They will snap and they will crackle, but they may no longer pop, as Kellogg’s has removed rice from its Rice Krispies and Coco Pops cereals due to “changing weather conditions”. Rice Krispies has been reformulated to use rice flour instead of rice, while Coco Pops now contain a blend of rice flour and corn flour instead of rice in order to maintain consistent quality. items.title: Consumer inflation falls to 9.6pc in Oct from 10.3pc in Sept
items.desc: ISLAMABAD: Consumer inflation eased to 9.6 per cent in October from 10.3pc a month earlier , mainly due to a slight slowdown in perishable food products, the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics said on Monday. The slowdown in the inflation rate for the second consecutive month, measured by the Consumer Price Index, reversed the sharp increase recorded in August , when higher food and energy prices pushed the annual rate to 11.1pc from 9.2pc in July. The easing was recorded in both places, in rural areas where inflation fell to 9.5pc from 10.1pc, while urban inflation edged down to 9.8pc from 10.5pc.
